source_text: if that person will not listen to you nor feel sorry that he has sinned against you, go get one or two other people who will listen to what you both have to say. have them go with you so that what is written {moses wrote} in the scriptures might happen: ‘when one person accuses another in some matter, it should be confirmed by at least two or three people {at least two or three people should confirm it} before that person can be declared guilty {before they declare that person guilty}. '
target_text: te ngaa ladhe no'o boe sèmi nare lii padhai èu, lamu paroa more angalai mu ca dhèu do dua dhèu, ho lami paraga dènge ne, sèna ka padhai lii hari. te ètu d'ara sasuri mola-mèci ama lamatua dhu suri tèke, peka na, ‘ètu d'ara lii langu èci, hud'i abhu ku dua-tèlu sakasii dhu lii èci, heka sèmi rare lii galaa ra. '

source_text: if the one who has sinned against you will not listen to them or does not feel sorry that he has sinned against you, tell that to the congregation so that they can rebuke him. if that person will not listen to the congregation or feel sorry that he has sinned against you, exclude him from being a member of your congregation, just like you would exclude pagans, tax collectors, and others who do not believe in god and sin greatly.
target_text: te ngaa ladhe no'o boe nanene lii miu, lami lole dènge juma'at. aa ladhe na d'èi boe nanene lii juma'at kahèi, tao ne nuka sèmi ca dhèu dhu tadhe boe lamatua. ladhe aad'o na, cap ne nuka sèmi dhèu bhelu, conto sèmi dhèu roro bea sèra.

source_text: keep this in mind: whatever you decide on earth about punishing or not punishing a member of your congregation is what has also been decided by god in heaven {what god in heaven has also decided}.
target_text: sanèd'e paie-iie lii padhai ja'a ne! ngaa dhu miu oro ètu rai-haha ne, èèna ka dhu lamatua oro le ètu sorga. aa ngaa dhu miu hia isin ètu rai-haha ne, èèna ka lamatua hia le isin ètu sorga kahèi.

source_text: also note this: if at least two of you who live here on earth agree together about something you ask god for dou, god, my father who is in heaven, will give you what you ask for.
target_text: aa ja'a peka hari, na, ladhe abhu dhèu dua dhu sabaj'a dènge d'ara èci, pe ama ku ètu sorga hia ngaa dhu ra manèngi.

source_text: this is true, because wherever at least two or three of you assemble because you believe in me mty, i am spiritually present with you. i will hear what you ask for and i will ask god to do it for you.
target_text: te, ladhe abhu dua, do tèlu dhèu, pakaboko sabaj'a sama-sama, lula rèngu dhèu ja'a, na, ja'a ètu talora aae rèngu kahèi.

source_text: then peter approached jesus and said to him, how many times must i forgive a fellow believer who keeps on sinning against me? if he keeps asking me to forgive him, must i forgive him as many as seven times?
target_text: èle èèna, ka petrus karèi yesus, aku nèngu na, ama, ja'a neo karèi ciki. ladhe a'ari ja'a tao sale pahari-pahari mi ja'a, èèna na d'ai pèri hari ja'a hud'i hia ne abho? d'ai pidhu hari, do?

source_text: jesus said to him, i tell you that the number of times you must forgive someone is not just up to seven, but you must ◄forgive him 77 times/never stop forgiving him►.
target_text: hèia yesus dhaa, peka na, aad'o! èu hud'i abho ne pidhu kali pidhu nguru hari, toke èu ige more heka.

source_text: in order to illustrate why you should do this, i will tell you a story in which god mty/eup, who cares for the people whose lives he rules over, is compared {i compare god, who cares for the people whose lives he rules over} to a king and his officials. that king told some of his servants that he wanted his officials to pay what they owed him.
target_text: miu hud'i tao ku sèmi èèna, lula ama lamatua nuka sèmi dhèu aae dhu ige kèlu na ètu pegawi na.

source_text: so those officials were brought to the king to settle their accounts with him. one of the officials who were brought owed the king several million dollars.
target_text: ropa na ige nare, hèia na pua dhèu lasi paroa pegawi dhu pakèlu toke riho kehi.

source_text: but because he did not have enough money to pay what he owed, the king demanded that he, his wife, his children and all he possessed be sold to someone else, and that the king be repaid with {receive} the money that was paid for them.
target_text: te ngaa pegawi ne b'ae nare boe kèlu na. ka dhèu aae paredha, peka na, ‘lami pahie eele dhèu ne dènge bhèni-ana niki na aa'i-aa'i, sèna ka ra j'aj'i ènu. aa mèdha-panyau na, pahie aa'i kahèi, ho b'ae kèlu-g'ètu na. '

source_text: then that official, knowing that he did not have the money to pay that huge debt, fell on his knees in front of the king and begged him saying, ‘be patient with me, and i will pay you all of it, eventually. '
target_text: ropa pegawi ne tadèngi nare, hèia na pabèbha iisi, ho patitu kètu urutuu ètu madha dhèu aae, ka pamako, aku nèngu na, ‘ira ee! ama dhèu aae hia ja'a tebho d'ai ciki sa! sèna ka ja'a b'ae kèlu ja'a aa'i-aa'i ra. '

source_text: the king, knowing that the official could never pay all that huge debt, felt sorry for him. so he canceled his debt and released him.
target_text: ropa tadèngi, hèia dhèu aae rasa kasia dènge ne. ka dhèu aae pabhèlu eele aa'i mèu-mèu kèlu na, ka pua na lèpa.

source_text: then this official went to another one of the king's officials who owed him a bit less than a year's wages. he grabbed him by the throat, started choking him, and said to him, ‘pay back what you owe me! '
target_text: te ngaa ropa na d'ai li'u, hèia pegawi ne paraga dènge angalai na dhu pakèlu nèngu doi ciki di. ka na kèpe angalai ne, hèia pacèli ladha goro na, aa na jèke ne, aku nèngu na, ‘weh! b'ae ka d'ara lai-lai ne kèlu èu sèra! '

source_text: that official fell on his knees and begged him saying, ‘be patient with me, and i will pay you all of it, eventually. '
target_text: ropa angalai na tadèngi, hèia na patitu kètu urutuu, ka pamako ne, peka na, ‘ira ee! angalai, ee! hia ku ja'a tebho d'ai ciki sa! pe ja'a b'ae kèlu ja'a sèra! '

source_text: but this official kept refusing to cancel that small debt that the man owed him. instead, he caused that official to be put in prison and to stay there until he could pay back all the money that he owed him.
target_text: te ngaa pegawi ne peka na, ‘bisa boe! ja'a mate heka panèbhu. èu b'ae dènge ka lod'o doe ne'e kahèi! ' èle ka, la'e pamaso angalai na asa d'ara bèdho, toke na b'ae aa'i kèlu na.

source_text: when the other officials of the king learned that this had happened, they felt very distressed. so they went to the king and reported in detail what had happened.
target_text: ropa pegawi dhu leo ladhe rèdhi ngaa dhu j'aj'i ne, hèia d'ara ra susa. ka lasi lolo dènge dhèu aae.

source_text: then the king summoned the official who had owed him several million dollars. he said to him, ‘you wicked servant! i canceled that huge debt that you owed me because you begged me to do so
target_text: ropa tadèngi nare, hèia dhèu aae ne paroa pegawi dhu ne'a boe manèngi makasi ne. dhèu aae jèke ne, aku nèngu na, ‘heh, dhèu bhelu-katub'a! lula èu ne manèngi sèna ka ja'a sue èu, nèti èèna ka ja'a pabhèlu eele le kèlu èu sèra.

source_text: you should have been merciful and canceled your fellow official's debt, just like i was merciful to you and canceled your debt rhq! '
target_text: te ngaa, nga tao ka èu kasia boe angalai èu sa hèi, sama sèmi ja'a kasia èu ne? '

source_text: the king was very angry. he handed this official over to some jailers who would torture him severely until he paid all of the debt that he owed.
target_text: ka dhèu aae nasa bia dènge ne, hèia na pua pamaso dhèu ne asa d'ara bèdho, sèna ka ra paj'èra ne, toke na b'ae aa'i kèlu na sèra.

source_text: then jesus continued by saying, that is what my father in heaven will do to you if you do not feel merciful and sincerely forgive a fellow believer who sins against you.
target_text: hèia yesus pa'èle lii pakasame na, peka na, ama ku ètu sorga pa'iga sèmi èèna kahèi mi dedha miu. pe na huku miu, ladhe miu mo'o boe pabhèlu eele sasala nèti a'ari miu dhèu parcaya sèra.

source_text: after jesus had said that, he took us and left galilee district and went to the part of judea district that is located on the east side of the jordan river.
target_text: ropa yesus aj'a nare aa'i j'ara sèra, hèia la'e tèke eele galilea asa propensi yudea, ètu cabèka loko yarden.

source_text: large crowds followed him there, and he healed the sick among them.
target_text: dhèu ae ka dhu madhutu ne, ka na puri-pa'èle dhèu-dhèu pèd'a ètu nèi.

source_text: some pharisees approached jesus and said to him, does our jewish law permit a man to divorce his wife for any reason whatever? they asked that in order to be able to criticize jesus, whether he answered yes or no.
target_text: abhu pèri-pèri dhèu parisi dhu madhutu kahèi, dhu neo pamanahu ne. ka ra karèi yesus, peka na, ama! madhutu atora agama èdhi, ladhe dhèu mone leo le èmu, bisa ia eele dhèu èmu na, sad'i na abhu j'ara dhu la'e asa pa'ie-pa'ela. sèmi èèna, do?

source_text: jesus said to them, because you have read rhq the scriptures, you should know that at the time god first created people, ‘he made one man, and he made one woman to be that man's wife. '
target_text: te ngaa yesus b'ala si, na miu se dhu me'a mèu agama. te ngaa tasamia ka miu me'a boe isi sasuri mola-mèci ama lamatua? te ètu d'ara sasuri nèti lii lolo uru tèka, dhu suri peka na, ‘ama lamatua paj'aj'i dhèu rai-haha, dhèu mone dènge dhèu bhèni. '

source_text: that explains why god said, ‘when a man and woman marry, they should no longer live with their fathers and mothers. instead, the two of them shall live together, and they shall become so closely united that they are like one person met. '
target_text: aa dhu suri kahèi, peka na, ‘nèti èèna ka, dhèu mone hud'i tèke eele ina-ama na, sèna ka la'e mamuri d'ara èci dènge dhèu èmu-kamali na, te dua ra dhu j'aj'i le èci. '

source_text: consequently, although they functioned as two separate people before, they now become as if they were one person met. since that is true, a man must not separate from his wife whom god has joined to him, because it is god's plan for them to remain together.
target_text: nèti èèna ka, ladhe ama lamatua unu na dhu hia dua ra j'aj'i le èci, na, dhèu rai-haha baku pacèri si hari!

source_text: the pharisees then said to him, if that is true, why did moses command that a man who wanted to divorce his wife should give her a paper stating his reason for divorcing her, and then send her away?
target_text: ropa tadèngi rare yesus peka sèmi èèna, dhèu parisi se karèi hari ne, peka na, ladhe sèmi èèna, nga tao ka musa peka na, dhèu bisa pa'ia-pa'ela, sad'i nèngu tao uuru ku sasuri pa'ia hia dhèu èmu na?

source_text: he said to them, it was because your ancestors stubbornly wanted their own way that moses allowed them to divorce their wives, and you are no different from them. but when god first mty created a man and a woman, he did not intend for them to separate.
target_text: hèia yesus dhaa, aku nèngu na, musa soro tèke bèi-baki miu pa'ia-pa'ela dènge dhèu èmu-kamali ra, lula rèngu sèra kètu hadhu èci èèna ka dènge miu! te ngaa lod'o ama lamatua paj'aj'i rai-haha ne, dad'èi na sèmi boe èèna.

source_text: i am telling you emphatically that because god considers that a marriage lasts until either the husband or the wife dies, he considers that any man who divorces his wife and marries another woman is committing adultery, unless his first wife has committed adultery.
target_text: nèti èèna ka, ja'a pasanèd'e mema miu, ee! ladhe bhèni ad'u uuru madha j'ara makae, dhèu èmu na bisa ia eele ne. te ngaa ladhe ia eele bhèni ne dhu ad'u boe j'ara makae, hèia dhèu mone na leo hari dènge bhèni leo, nèngu ne tao le j'ara makae!

source_text: we disciples said to him, if that is true, it is better for men never to marry!
target_text: ropa tadèngi lii ne'e, hèia ana madhutu na sèra, peka na, ladhe sèmi èèna, be'a risi baku leo-èmu.

source_text: then he said to us, not every man is able to accept this teaching. only the men whom god enables to accept it are able to do so.
target_text: hèia yesus b'ala si, aku nèngu na, dhèu ae ka dhu ro'o boe sèmi rare lii padhai lii ja'a ne. dhodhoka dhèu dhu ama lamatua hag'e nare si.

source_text: there are men who do not marry because they are not able to have sexual relations because they have been sexually defective ever since they were born. there are other men who do not marry because they are unable to have sexual relations because they have been castrated {other men have made them that way}. there are other men who decide not to marry met in order that they can serve god better and spend more time telling people about how god mty/eup wants to rule people's lives. you who are able to understand what i have said about marriage should accept it and obey it.
target_text: te abhu dhèu dhu leo boe èmu, lula karèi nèti rara iisi ne, nèngu sèmi èèna ka. abhu kahèi dhu leo boe èmu, lula dhèu tao ne sèmi èèna. aa abhu kahèi dhu no'o boe leo-èmu, lula na neo pakako sasab'a ama lamatua di. dhèu dhu re'a mèu a'aj'a ne, hud'i laa nèngu sèmi dènge be'a.

source_text: then some children were brought {some people brought their children} to jesus in order that he might lay his hands on them and pray for them. but we disciples scolded the people for bringing their children to jesus because we thought that jesus did not want to take the time to be with children.
target_text: lod'o èèna, dhèu sa'u rèti ana-ana ra asa yesus, sèna ka yesus tao kacui-aai na mi rèngu, aa dènge hia lii mèngi-nale. te ngaa ana madhutu na kai dhèu se.

source_text: but when jesus saw us scolding them, he said to us, let the children come to me! do not stop them! it is people who are humble and trusting like they are, who can experience god's rule in their lives.
target_text: hèia yesus nasa dènge ana madhutu na, ka na lii, aku nèngu na, hud'i laa ana se mai asa ja'a! baku bhabhae si! te dhèu dhu sèmi rèngu se'e ka, dhu j'aj'i dhèu unu ama lamatua.

source_text: jesus then laid his hands on the children and asked god to bless them. then he left there.
target_text: èle èèna ka yesus tao kacui-aai na mi ana se, aa na manèngi ho ama lamatua hia si mèngi-nale. èle, hèia yesus pakèd'i la'e, tèke eele era èèna.

source_text: as jesus was walking along, a young man approached him and said to him, teacher, what good deeds must i do in order to live with god eternally?
target_text: ca tèke, dhèu èci mai karèi yesus, peka na, ama mese! ja'a hud'i tao ku j'ara dhu hua iia tasamia, sèna ka ke'a tare'a, na, ja'a bisa maso sorga? te ja'a neo mamuri taruu sama-sama dènge ama lamatua.

source_text: jesus said to him, ◄consider what you are implying about who i am when you ask me about what is good. /do you realize what you are implying about who i am when you ask me about that which is good? ► rhq only one being is good and really knows what is good. that being is god. but in order to answer your question about desiring to live with god eternally, i will say to you, ‘keep the commandments that god gave moses'.
target_text: hèia yesus dhaa, peka na, nga tao ka, èu karèi ja'a lula-nèti ngaa dhu hua iia? dhodhoka ama lamatua di, dhu hua iia. te ladhe èu neo mamuri taruu dènge ne, na, mamuri la madhutu paredha na.

source_text: the man asked jesus, which commandments must i keep? jesus answered him, do not murder anyone, do not commit adultery, do not steal things, do not testify falsely,
target_text: ka dhèu ne karèi hari, aku nèngu na, paredha dhu mia èèna? hèia yesus b'ala ne, peka na, baku pamadhe dhèu; baku tao j'ara makae dènge dhèu dhu dhèu èmu boe èu; baku mana'u; baku j'aj'i sakasii dhu kapod'e-kabèli;

source_text: honor your father and your mother, and love people you come in contact with as much as you love yourself.
target_text: pakab'ua ina-ama mu; aa sue ku dhèu èu, sama sèmi èu sue ngi'u èu mesa mu.

source_text: thinking that he might not be able to live with god eternally even though he had kept those commandments, the young man said to jesus, i have always obeyed all those commandments. what else must i do in order to live with god eternally?
target_text: dhèu ne dhaa, na, paredha aa'i-aa'i sèra ja'a tao madhutu le. de, ngaa hari dhu kura?

source_text: jesus said to him, if you desire to be all that god intends you to be, go home, sell everything that you have and give the money to poor people. the result will be that you will have spiritual riches in heaven. then come and be my disciple!
target_text: ropa tadèngi lii dhèu ne, hèia yesus peka na, ladhe èu neo madhutu aa'i dad'èi ama lamatua, lèpa ho pahia aa'i mèdha-panyau èu, sèna ka papala hia dhèu dhu dènge boe ngaa-ngaa sèra. èle èèna, mai ho madhutu ja'a. te èèna na, ama lamatua pala hia èu mèdha-panyau ae-ae ètu sorga.

source_text: when the young man heard those words, he went away feeling sad, because he was very rich and did not want to give away everything he owned.
target_text: ropa na tadèngi nare lii yesus, hèia dhèu ne lèpa dènge d'ara pèd'a laho mae-mae, lula nèngu kaja titu kèna.

source_text: then jesus said to us disciples, keep this in mind: it is very difficult for rich people to decide to let god mty/eup rule their lives.
target_text: èle èèna, ka yesus padhai lii dènge ana madhutu na, aku nèngu na, lèka la ja'a, te dhèu kaja carui titu kèna maso sorga.

source_text: note this also: it is impossible for a camel to go through the eye of a needle. it is almost as difficult hyp for rich people to decide to let god rule their lives.
target_text: carui èèna, nuka sèmi badha onta dhu kapai, maso la'e asa d'ara oka na re ro'a j'aj'au.

source_text: when we disciples heard this, we were astounded. we thought that rich people were the ones whom god blesses the most. so we said to him, ◄if that is so, it does not seem likely that anyone will be saved! /who then will god will save? ► rhq
target_text: ropa ana madhutu se tadèngi rare, rèngu malaa, hèia ra dhaa, peka na, ladhe sèmi èèna, cee ka dhu bisa maso sorga?

source_text: when jesus heard us say that, he looked intently at us, and then he said to us, yes, it is impossible for people to save themselves. but god can save them, because god is able to do anything!
target_text: hèia yesus ladhe patae si, ka na lii, peka na, ladhe dhèu rai-haha dhu tao, mema bisa boe. te ngaa ladhe ama lamatua ka dhu tao, aa'i-aa'i bisa j'aj'i!

source_text: then peter said to him, you know that we exc have left everything behind and we have become your disciples. so what benefit will we get for doing that?
target_text: hèia petrus pasanèd'e, aku nèngu na, ama! ji'i se tèke eele le mèdha-panyau ji'i aa'i-aa'i, ho madhutu ama. de ji'i abhu ngaa?

source_text: jesus said to us, keep this in mind: you will get many benefits. when god makes the new earth and when i, the one who came from heaven, sit on my magnificent throne, those of you who have accompanied me will each sit on a throne, and you will judge the people of the twelve tribes of israel.
target_text: na dhaa, peka na, parcaya la ja'a ne! pe d'ai lod'o ama lamatua tao pahiu aa'i mèu-mèu, ja'a dhèu rai-haha tare'a-re'a ne, madhèdi ètu dedha kadera paredha aae èèna. lod'o èèna kahèi, miu dhu madhutu ja'a, madhèdi kahèi ètu dedha kadera paredha canguru dua sèra, sèna ka j'aj'i hakim mi canguru dua suku èdhi dhèu isra'el!

source_text: god will reward those who, because of being my disciples, have left behind a house or plot of ground, their brothers, their sisters, their father, their mother, their children, or any other family mty members. god will give them 100 times as many benefits as they have given up. and they will live with god eternally.
target_text: dhèu dhu tèke eele èmu na, a'ari na, ina-ama na, ana niki na, aa oka-tedhe na, ho madhutu ja'a, bèli-camèd'a èèna abhu hari cangasu kali. aa d'ai ka lod'o èle rai-haha ne, nèngu kahèi abhu mamuri taruu dènge ama lamatua.

source_text: but many people who consider themselves to be important now will be unimportant at that future time, and many people who consider themselves to be unimportant now will be important at that future time.
target_text: de sanèd'e paie! madhutu ngangee ama lamatua, dhèu ae dhu padedha iisi na, rèngu sèra ka dhu j'aj'i mi ana iiki. te ngaa dhèu dhu peka na, nèngu dhèu haha, aa te ngaa madhutu a'abhu lamatua, nèngu ka dhu kapai.

source_text: in order to illustrate how god rewards people, i will compare the way god mty/eup rules his people with what the owner of an estate did. early in the morning the owner of the estate went to the market where people who wanted work gathered. he went there to hire laborers to work in his vineyard.
target_text: èle èèna, ka yesus aj'a peka na, paredha ama lamatua èci èèna ka dènge lii pakasame ne: abhu ca dhèu lamatua oka anggor, dhu kèd'i mad'ae aae d'ara hake èna sa. na la'e tenge dhèu sèna ka sab'a ètu d'ara oka na.

source_text: he promised the men whom he hired that he would pay them the standard wage for working one day. then he sent them to his vineyards.
target_text: na abhu dhèu sab'a, hèia rare lii èci, ho sab'e d'ara ca lod'o, bab'ae na, ca doi iia. dhèu se d'èi kahèi, ka lamatua oka ne pua lasi sab'a.

source_text: at nine o'clock that same morning he went back to the market. there he saw more men who did not have work.
target_text: pe d'ara hake ceo sa, la'e asa d'ara pasa. ètu era nèi, nèngu paraga dènge dhèu pèri-pèri dhu madhèdi iia d'ara.

source_text: he said to them, ‘go to my vineyard as other men have done, and work there. i will pay you whatever is a just wage. ' so they also went to his vineyard and began to work.
target_text: hèia na lii dènge ra, ‘miu se neo sab'a ètu d'ara oka ja'a, do? pe ja'a b'ae miu madhutu kab'ua dhu lèke. ' ropa tadèngi rare, ro'o kahèi, hèia lasi dènge ka sab'a.

source_text: at noon and at three o'clock he again went to the market and found other laborers whom he promised to pay a fair wage.
target_text: d'ai lod'o titu mera sa, dènge hake tèlu lod'o nihia, lamatua oka ne la'e tenge hari dhèu sab'a.

source_text: at five o'clock he went to the market again and saw other men standing there who were not working. he said to them, ‘why are you standing here all day and not working? '

source_text: o people of jerusalem mty, apo, you killed the prophets who lived long ago, and you killed others whom god sent to you. you killed them by throwing stones at them dou! many times i wanted to gather you together to protect you, like a hen gathers her young chicks under her wings met. but you did not want me to do that.

source_text: jesus left the temple courtyard. as he was walking along, we disciples came to him to ask him to note how beautiful the temple buildings were.

target_text: te ngaa yesus peka dènge ra, na, èmu ne, mema saraga. te ngaa nanene, ee! nèbhu heka dhèu mai paguri eele aa'i hadhu se.

source_text: later, as jesus was sitting alone on the slope of olive tree hill, we disciples went to him and asked him, when will this happen to the buildings of the temple? also, tell us what will happen to indicate that you are about to come again, and to indicate that this world is ending?
target_text: hèia yesus la'e madhèdi asa ledhe saitun. ka ana madhutu na mai padhai lii mesa ra dènge ne, peka na, ama! peka hari ku laa, lii padhai ama deo na. j'aj'aj'i na pèri lod'o? mamai hari ama na lod'o mia? aa tadha-tadha na tasamia? tasamia kahèi dènge lod'o èle rai-haha?

source_text: jesus replied, all that i will say is, be sure that no one deceives you about what will happen
target_text: ka yesus dhaa, peka na, j'aga paie mamuri miu, sèna ka dhèu baku kapod'e-kabèli miu.

source_text: you will hear about wars that are close and wars that are far away, but do not let that trouble you. keep in mind that god has said that those things must happen. but when they happen, it will not mean that the end of the world has come!
target_text: ladhe miu mèdhi ka, dhèu pamusu, do, tadèngi lii palolo dhèu papara-pakèj'i ètu mia-mia, na, miu baku madha'u kahèi. te j'ara se'e se, hud'i j'aj'i uuru ku, te ngaa lod'o èle rai-haha ne dhae d'ai mèka.

source_text: groups in various countries will fight each other, and various governments will also fight against each other. there will be famines and earthquakes in various places.
target_text: dhèu nèti ca suku, èèna na pamusu dènge suku leo. negara èci pamusu, lab'a negara leo. ètu mia-mia abhu rai opo, aa manganga-mad'èu dhu kapai titu kèna.

source_text: these things will happen first. then there will be other things that will happen before i return. what will happen will be like the first pains of childbirth met.
target_text: te ngaa sèra sa, heka tadha partama kèna, dhu peka na, lod'o èle rai-haha dètu ae le. èèna nuka sèmi bhèni dhu mulai kabake pèd'a neo nara iisi.

source_text: at that time people who oppose you will take you to the authorities, who will mistreat you and kill you. you will be hated by people who live in all nations prs {people who live in all nations prs will hate you} because you believe in me mty.
target_text: de miu hud'i j'aga paie ku ngi'u miu! te bèli-camèd'a dhèu mai paj'èra dènge pamadhe miu. aa dhèu nèti suku aa'i-aa'i, èèna na d'èi boe miu, lula miu madhutu ja'a.

source_text: also, many people will stop believing in me because of the way they will suffer. they will betray each other and will hate each other.

source_text: because there will be more and more people who will disobey god's laws prs, many people will no longer met love their fellow believers prs.
target_text: bèli-camèd'a bhabhelu dhèu asa tabha, toke dhèu re'a heka pasue èci dènge èci.

source_text: but all those who keep on believing in me to the end of their lives will be saved.

source_text: furthermore, the good message about my ruling over people's lives will be preached in every part of the world, in order that people of all ethnic groups may hear it. then the end of the world will come.

source_text: but before the world ends, the disgusting person who will defile the holy temple and cause people to abandon it will stand in the temple. daniel the prophet spoke and wrote about that long ago. may everyone who reads this pay attention to the following warning from me:

source_text: it will be like what happened when noah lived. until the flood came, the people did not know that anything bad would happen to them. before the flood waters covered the earth, the people were eating and drinking as usual. some men were marrying women and some parents were giving their daughters to men to marry them. they were doing all this until the day that noah and his family entered the big boat. and then the flood came and drowned all those who were not in the boat. similarly, the unbelieving people will not know when i, the one who came from heaven, will return, and they will not be expecting me.
target_text: te ja'a ne, dhèu rai-haha tare'a-re'a. bèli-camèd'a ropa ja'a mai hari, nuka sèmi taa uru sèra, lod'o noh mamuri era. èi aae dhae j'aj'i mèka lala, te ngaa dhèu-dhèu dhu ra'a-rinu, aa paleo èmu sèmi biasa. dhèu sèra tao taruu sèmi èèna, toke noh maso asa d'ara kapa aae èèna. te ngaa ropa èi aae lala, hae nèti aa'i si, rèngu heka kabèdhi kèna, lula ngaa dhu j'aj'i sèra. èci èèna ka dènge mamai ja'a bèli-camèd'a.

source_text: when i return, i will not take all people up to heaven. i will take only those who trust in me. for example, two people will be in the fields. one of them will be taken {i will take one of them} up to heaven and the other person will be left {and i will leave the other person} here to be punished.
target_text: lod'o èèna, ladhe abhu dhèu dua ètu d'ara oka, cag'ag'a laa ama lamatua ded'e nèti ca dhèu, aa ca dhèu hari tèke eele.

target_text: ladhe dhèu bhèni dhèu dua dhu maj'u are, kaca'a la ama lamatua ded'e nèti ca dhèu, aa ca dhèu hari tèke eele.

source_text: so, because you do not know what day i, your lord, will return to the earth, you need to be ready for me to return at any time.
target_text: nèti èèna ka, miu hud'i bori pa'èra mema kahèi, te miu me'a boe pèri lod'o lamatua miu lèpa hari mai.

source_text: you know that if the owners of a house knew at what time in the night thieves would come, they would be awake and prevent the thieves from breaking into their houses. similarly, i will come just like unexpectedly as a thief.
target_text: pangee paie-iie! ladhe lamatua èmu dhu ne'a mema, na, mèda none dhèu mana'u mai, tatu na pasaruru boe musi madha na, sèna ka dhèu mana'u baku maso asa d'ara èmu.

source_text: so you need to be ready for my return, because i, the one who came from heaven, will return to the earth at a time when you do not expect me to come.
target_text: nèti èèna ka, miu hud'i pa'èra mema kahèi. te mamai hari ja'a èèna, dènge sahèka!

source_text: think about what every faithful and wise servant is like rhq. the house owner appoints one servant to supervise the other servants. he tells him to give them food at the proper times. then he leaves on a long trip.
target_text: ka yesus tuhu hari lii padhai na, peka na, miu hud'i j'aj'i ku nuka sèmi dhèu sab'a dhu madhutu dhodhoka dad'èi lamatua na. te ladhe lamatua na neo la'e rai kaj'èu, na ded'e dhèu sab'a dhu sèmi èèna ku, ho uri nganga'a-nganginu hia isi èmu na.

source_text: if that servant is doing that work when the house owner returns, the house owner will be very pleased with him.

source_text: but a wicked servant might say to himself, ‘the owner has been away for a long time, so he probably will not return soon and find out what i am doing. '

source_text: so he will begin to beat the other servants and eat and get drunk.
target_text: ‘be'a kèna! lamatua ja'a la'e le, de cee ne'a na pèri lod'o lèpa hari mai! ' nèti ngangee sèmi ne'e ne, hèia na kalabhe dhèu sab'a leo sèra. aa nèngu madhèdi na'a-ninu mau-mau bera-bera dènge dhèu mahu sèra.

source_text: then the house owner will come back at a time when the servant does not expect him dou.
target_text: te ngaa dhu ne'a nare boe, na, cag'ag'a laa lamatua na lèpa hari mai.
